content.comment_body: Hello, I seem to be experiencing a similar issue. When attempting to transfer the program from my PC to the [product_name], a password is required, but I haven't set one. My hardware is [company_name] [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. The software is [product_name] version [version_no] (licensed full version). What could be causing this?

I'm not sure why a password is being requested. If your [product_name]'s firmware is [version_no], that's a specific version requiring a newer software version, at least [version_no]. If you have a full license, upgrading to [version_no] is free. Please refer to the relevant FAQ for guidance on why program downloads might not work with your new [product_name].
That's correct—with an older [product_name] (firmware [version_no]), everything works fine. I'll need to upgrade and will update you. Thanks a lot.
Is there an official source or link for the [version_no] upgrade?
All of this information is available in the FAQ linked in my previous post.
The steps described in the FAQ ('Why can you not download any programs into your new [product_name]?') aren't working for me. *[product_name] *Help *Update Center
Could it be that you already have [version_no]? Click on Help > About and take a screenshot.

Alternatively, you can obtain the upgrade from the following location: Demo software, upgrades/updates, drivers. Ensure you are using either a 32-bit or 64-bit operating system. After downloading, run 'Setup.exe' as an administrator, which is essential.

Hi, I've downloaded the installer for the Windows 64-bit upgrade [product_name] to [version_no], and switched my network connection from 'Broadcom9432...HML wifi 2x2 adapter' to 'Realtek PCIe GBE Fam Controller.' The PC-to-[product_name] transfer was successful. Thanks!
Yes, when I open the upgraded [product_name], it shows [version_no]. The other files downloaded earlier were demo versions.
Editing posts after a response can make it harder to follow the conversation. It's better to create a new post for clarity.

I usually edit small mistakes to keep things readable, especially when mixing languages, but I understand your point and will keep it in mind. Back to the [product_name] version issue: to get the latest version, go to the following source: Demo software, upgrades/updates, drivers. Pick the appropriate file for the upgrade. To update [product_name], select the upgrade path from earlier versions up to [version_no]. The new [version_no] will install separately. The older version is still available if needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced a password prompt when trying to transfer a program from a PC to a [product_name], despite not setting a password. The root issue was a compatibility mismatch between the module's firmware version and the management software. Resolving this required upgrading the software to support the firmware, which enabled successful program transfer. FAQ resources, upgrade procedures, and proper network settings figured prominently in achieving a solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward process for transferring programs from their PC to the [product_name] without unexpected password requests if no password is present. They expect the software to be compatible with the latest firmware and support easy upgrades.
